title: SmoothConvexConcave.lean

problem_class.label: saddle_point
problem_class.details: Minimize in x and maximize in y a differentiable convex-concave function φ over X×Y; no strong convexity or strong concavity is assumed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query z=(x,y) returns (∇xφ(x,y),−∇yφ(x,y)) exactly. Gradient uniqueness removes dependence on call index and oracle seed; no function values are supplied.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E and F are complete real inner-product spaces, with no finite-dimensional restriction. X and Y are nonempty compact convex sets; the product-domain diameter is at most D≥0. The saddle-gradient map is globally L-Lipschitz, with L>0. All parameters, spaces and constraint sets are public; φ is the hidden instance. The target ε>0 is public. Only oracle calls are budgeted, with fixed cost O(1+LD²/ε); other operations are unrestricted.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothConvexConcave.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.valid, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Setup.allowedAlgorithm, Convergence; supplied OracleTemplate.SaddlePoint.result budget

accuracy.label: saddle_point_gap
accuracy.details: The measurable output z satisfies E[sup(y∈Y)φ(z.1,y)−inf(x∈X)φ(x,z.2)]≤ε, and this gap is integrable. No last-iterate requirement is imposed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The gap bound is in expectation under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law; deterministic accuracy is not required.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The output belongs to X×Y almost surely; this probability guarantee applies to feasibility.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is the standard smooth convex-concave constrained saddle-point formulation with an exact Lipschitz first-order oracle and expected primal-dual gap accuracy, stated in real Hilbert spaces.

descriptionHtml:
Smooth Convex–Concave Saddle Problems

We consider a convex–concave function φ:E×F→R on real Hilbert spaces E,F, with nonempty compact convex feasible sets X⊆E and Y⊆F. Their product has diameter at most D≥0 in the maximum product norm. The oracle returns G(x,y)=(∇xφ(x,y),−∇yφ(x,y)), which exists everywhere and is globally L-Lipschitz for L>0. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output (x¯,y¯)∈X×Y almost surely with integrable primal–dual gap and EP[supy∈Yφ(x¯,y)−infx∈Xφ(x,y¯)]≤ε, where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The saddle-point problem is minx∈Xmaxy∈Yφ(x,y). We equip the product space with the norm ∥(x,y)∥=max{∥x∥E,∥y∥F}, where the component norms are induced by the Hilbert inner products. The algorithm receives E,F,X,Y,L,D, and ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Feasible geometry). The sets X and Y are nonempty, compact, and convex, and ∥z−w∥≤D,z,w∈X×Y.

Assumption 2 (Convexity and concavity). For every x,x′∈X, y,y′∈Y, and t∈[0,1], φ((1−t)x+tx′,y)≤(1−t)φ(x,y)+tφ(x′,y),φ(x,(1−t)y+ty′)≥(1−t)φ(x,y)+tφ(x,y′).

Assumption 3 (Global smoothness). For every (x,y)∈E×F, the functions φ(⋅,y) and φ(x,⋅) are Fréchet differentiable at x and y, respectively. Their signed gradient map satisfies ∥G(z)−G(w)∥≤L∥z−w∥,z,w∈E×F.

Queries may be made at any point of E×F, and each oracle reply is the exact signed gradient G(x,y). Define the primal–dual gap by Gap(x,y)=supv∈Yφ(x,v)−infu∈Xφ(u,y). After the allotted oracle calls, the output (x¯,y¯) must be measurable with respect to the given measurable structures on E and F, and must satisfy (x¯,y¯)∈X×YP-a.s.,EP[|Gap(x¯,y¯)|]<∞,EP[Gap(x¯,y¯)]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
Nonempty compact convex sets X⊂E, Y⊂F in real Hilbert spaces have product diameter at most D≥0. The function φ:E×F→R is convex–concave on X×Y, with partial gradients everywhere; the exact oracle G=(∇xφ,−∇yφ) is globally L-Lipschitz, L>0. For ε>0, the target is a feasible output with ∫Gap(z(ω))dP(ω)≤ε. Result (1) constructs deterministic projected extragradient with step 1/(2L) and averages its extrapolated points; its gap is at most ε for every seed.

Smooth convex–concave saddle points: SmoothConvexConcave.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) SmoothConvexConcave (Ours) (review) O(1+LD2/ε) exact G calls; one product projection per call.
(2) Mirror-Prox (Nemirovski 2004, Thm. 3.2, (3.10)). Euclidean specialization; finite dimensions. O(1+LD2/ε) exact G calls; one product projection per call. (1): Matches known rate on finite-dimensional overlap; Lean formalization. Scope: compact subsets of Hilbert spaces instead of finite-dimensional spaces. (1) needs ambient differentiability and Lipschitz continuity; (2) needs them only on X×Y. No general Bregman-geometry guarantee in (1).
(3) Lower bound (Ouyang and Xu 2018, Thm. 9). Bilinearly coupled problems on Euclidean balls. Ω(LD2/ε) calls in the regime Lf=∥A∥≍L, RX≍RY≍D, LD2/ε≫1. Oracle: (∇f(x),Ax,A⊤y). (1) matches the worst-case order for deterministic first-order methods when 8<m≤n and the call horizon satisfies t<m/4−2.

Abbr: Gap(x,y)=supv∈Yφ(x,v)−infu∈Xφ(u,y); P is the execution probability law. L,D use the max product norm ∥(x,y)∥=max{∥x∥,∥y∥}. A product projection projects onto X and Y. In (3), φ(x,y)=f(x)+⟨Ax−b,y⟩, Lf is the Lipschitz constant of ∇f, RX,RY are ball radii, n,m their dimensions, and t the oracle-call horizon; Ω denotes a lower bound, ≍ equality up to universal factors.

Nemirovski, Arkadi. 2004. “Prox-Method with Rate of Convergence O(1/t) for Variational Inequalities with Lipschitz Continuous Monotone Operators and Smooth Convex-Concave Saddle Point Problems.” SIAM Journal on Optimization 15 (1): 229–51. https://doi.org/10.1137/S1052623403425629.
Ouyang, Yuyuan, and Yangyang Xu. 2018. Lower Complexity Bounds of First-Order Methods for Convex-Concave Bilinear Saddle-Point Problems. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1808.02901.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.SmoothConvexConcave

open OracleTemplate

noncomputable def gap (E F : Type*) (X : Set E) (Y : Set F) (φ : E → F → ℝ) (z : E × F) : ℝ :=
  sSup ((fun y => φ z.1 y) '' Y) - sInf ((fun x => φ x z.2) '' X)

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  F : Type u
  [normedF : NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [linearF : InnerProductSpace ℝ F]
  [completeF : CompleteSpace F]
  [measurableF : MeasurableSpace F]
  L : ℝ
  D : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  X : Set E
  Y : Set F

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE Params.measurableE Params.normedF Params.linearF Params.completeF Params.measurableF

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → p.F → ℝ
  Query p := p.E × p.F
  Reply p := p.E × p.F
  Output p := p.E × p.F
  publicInput p := p
  valid q :=
    0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.D ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧
    q.X.Nonempty ∧ q.Y.Nonempty ∧ IsCompact q.X ∧ IsCompact q.Y ∧
    Convex ℝ q.X ∧ Convex ℝ q.Y ∧
    (∀ z ∈ q.X ×ˢ q.Y, ∀ w ∈ q.X ×ˢ q.Y, ‖z - w‖ ≤ q.D)
  admissible q φ O :=
    (∀ y ∈ q.Y, ConvexOn ℝ q.X (fun x => φ x y)) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ q.X, ConcaveOn ℝ q.Y (φ x)) ∧
    (∀ k seed z, HasGradientAt (fun x => φ x z.2) (O.answer k (0, z) seed).1 z.1 ∧
      HasGradientAt (φ z.1) (-(O.answer k (0, z) seed).2) z.2) ∧
    (∀ k seed z w, ‖O.answer k (0, z) seed - O.answer k (0, w) seed‖ ≤ q.L * ‖z - w‖)
  successful q φ output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), output ω ∈ q.X ×ˢ q.Y) ∧
    Integrable (fun ω => gap q.E q.F q.X q.Y φ (output ω)) (P : Measure _) ∧
    (∫ ω, gap q.E q.F q.X q.Y φ (output ω) ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.SmoothConvexConcave
